comparison.objective: Assemble and tighten a pipe compression joint in the correct part order; candidate adjusts and locks a shock absorber based on repeated dynamic trials.
comparison.physical_skill: Compression joint tests pipe seating, ordered olive/nut placement, spanner-on-flats alignment, repeated short tightening strokes, and tool return. Candidate tests recessed hex-key insertion, collar counterholding and fine rotation, relocking, control actuation, and feedback-driven retuning.
comparison.success_condition: Joint requires pipe within 1 mm of its stop, olive under the nut, and 0.75–1.25 turns past snug without over-compression. Candidate requires two safe ≥0.85 J stops, ≤12 mm travel, no hard-stop/rebound/overload, and limited post-lock drift.
comparison.reason: Shared tool alignment and bounded rotation are generic primitives. The joint primarily tests assembly order, concentric insertion, and controlled make-up; the candidate tests iterative calibration of physical dynamics. Joint fidelity has no torque or real olive compression and uses guided rings/code threads; candidate lacks numeric drift tolerance and published tightening/damping calibration.
